description: Get formatted citations for PubMed articles in one or more formats (apa, mla, bibtex, ris, vancouver). Pass a single format as a string or multiple as an array. Retractions, errata, and expressions of concern NCBI links to an article come back in `notices`; Vancouver and APA also cite a retraction in the reference itself.

anyOf.description: Single citation style. One of: apa, mla, bibtex, ris, vancouver.
Multiple citation styles to generate. Each entry: apa, mla, bibtex, ris, or vancouver.

format.description: Citation format(s) to generate — single style as a string or multiple as an array. Allowed values: apa, mla, bibtex, ris, vancouver.

name: pubmed_format_citations

notices.description: Retraction, erratum, and expression-of-concern notices NCBI links to this article, in NCBI's order. Vancouver notes each `RetractionIn` and `ErratumIn` after the reference and APA each `RetractionIn`; the other types, and MLA, BibTeX, and RIS, carry none, so check this before citing. Absent when NCBI links none.

items.description: A linked notice that qualifies the cited article

note.description: NCBI's note on the link, e.g. the correction an erratum makes. Absent when NCBI gives none.

pmid.description: PMID of the notice — pass it to `pubmed_fetch_articles` to read it. Absent when the notice has no PMID, as with many errata.

refSource.description: Citation of the notice as NCBI writes it (e.g. "Lancet. 2010 Feb 6;375(9713):445. doi: 10.1016/S0140-6736(10)60175-4.").

refType.description: NCBI's `RefType` for the link: RetractionIn, RetractedandRepublishedIn, ExpressionOfConcernIn, ErratumIn, or CorrectedandRepublishedIn.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `queue_full`: The local NCBI request queue shed the call — the queue is full, or the call cannot start before its total deadline (for example behind the cooldown that follows an NCBI 429). `ncbi_unreachable`: NCBI E-utilities failed on every attempt the retry budget allowed — retries ran out, or the next backoff would overrun the total deadline. `ncbi_rate_limited`: NCBI answered HTTP 429 (too many requests) and the call stopped on it — retries ran out, the next backoff would overrun the total deadline, or the Retry-After NCBI named outlasts the time left or the 30-second backoff cap. `ncbi_deadline_exceeded`: The total NCBI request deadline expired before NCBI answered successfully — mid-request, while queued, or during a retry backoff. `ncbi_invalid_response`: NCBI returned a body that could not be parsed (invalid XML/JSON). `ncbi_resource_not_found`: NCBI returned a structured "not found" error for the requested ID(s). Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

notice.description: Optional guidance when no citations were produced — points to discovery tools. Absent when at least one citation was produced.

totalSubmitted.description: Number of PMIDs submitted for citation formatting

unavailablePmids.description: PMIDs PubMed returned no record for, so nothing could be cited for them. That is all this reports: PubMed omits a PMID it does not recognize silently, with no error and no reason, so the absence says nothing about whether the PMID exists. Use `pubmed_search_articles` to find PMIDs that do resolve.

title: Pubmed Format Citations
